subtitle: How a quiet investigation turned indigo fear into a record the Raj could not ignore

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of Gandhi standing in a dusty Champaran field, indigo shrubs around, faint outline of a planter bungalow and a distant courthouse on opposite horizons
panels.action: Mahatma Gandhi stands barefoot in a Champaran field, simple dhoti fluttering, as indigo plants rustle at his feet and, far behind him, a planter’s bungalow and a colonial courthouse loom on opposite sides like opposing forces.

dialogue.text: In 1917 Champaran, where indigo meant fear, Gandhi chose not a riot, but a notebook, and forced the Raj to read its own injustice.

i18n.hi: 1917 के चंपारण में, जहाँ नील मतलब डर था, गांधी ने दंगे नहीं, डायरी चुनी — और राज को उसकी अपनी नाइंसाफी पढ़वा दी।

panels.shot: interior wide of a modest ashram room in Calcutta/Patna, Gandhi seated on the floor as a determined peasant bows before him
panels.action: Inside a sparse room, Gandhi sits cross-legged on a mat, calm and slight, as a wiry peasant tenant, Raj Kumar Shukla, leans forward, eyes burning with urgency, clutching a worn cloth bundle.

dialogue.text: It began not in a court, but at Gandhi’s feet, when a persistent peasant, Raj Kumar Shukla, refused to stop asking him to see Champaran’s indigo sorrow.

i18n.hi: कचहरी से नहीं, गांधी के चरणों से शुरू हुआ, जब जिद्दी किसान राजकुमार शुक्ला ने चंपारण की नील की पीड़ा दिखाने की गुहार छोड़ने से इनकार कर दिया।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Gandhi and Shukla at a railway platform, steam around them, Shukla gripping Gandhi’s arm as the train waits
panels.action: On a crowded railway platform, smoke curling in the air, Raj Kumar Shukla grips Gandhi’s arm by a waiting train, his cracked feet on the dusty boards, while Gandhi listens, head slightly bowed, a small cloth bag in hand.

dialogue.speaker: Raj Kumar Shukla
dialogue.text: Bapu, come see our fields. Indigo has chained us.

i18n.hi: बापू, खेत देखिए। नील ने हमें जकड़ रखा है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the train rolling through the Gangetic plains, Gandhi looking out the window at flooded fields and distant huts
panels.action: A third-class carriage rattles through the flat Gangetic plains, Gandhi by the barred window, watching small thatched huts and waterlogged fields slide past under a wide, pale sky.

dialogue.text: Leaving Calcutta’s noise, Gandhi rode into north Bihar’s silence, carrying only a small bag and a larger question: could truth alone loosen a system built on indigo and fear?

i18n.hi: कलकत्ता की हलचल छोड़ गांधी उत्तर बिहार की खामोशी में घुसे, छोटा सा बस्ता लेकर, और बड़ा सवाल: क्या सिर्फ सच से नील और डर पर खड़ी यह जंजीर ढीली हो सकती है?

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of Champaran countryside showing scattered villages, indigo patches, and a distant planter factory chimney
panels.action: From above, the Champaran countryside stretches out: clusters of mud-brick huts, narrow paths between plots, patches of indigo crop, and far off a tall chimney of a planter’s factory rising over a line of trees.

dialogue.text: Champaran was not a battlefield, but a patchwork of estates where tenants, tied by tinkathia, had to grow indigo on fixed land even when the blue dye had lost its shine on world markets.

i18n.hi: चंपारण कोई मैदान-ए-जंग नहीं, बल्कि जमींदारियों की जाल थी, जहाँ किरायेदार टिंकठिया से बंधे, तय जमीन पर नील उगाने को मजबूर थे, जबकि नीला रंग दुनिया में अपनी चमक खो चुका था।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot inside a peasant hut, Gandhi seated on a low stool as a tenant couple speaks nervously
panels.action: Inside a dim hut lit by a single shaft of light, Gandhi perches on a low stool with a notebook on his knee, while a gaunt tenant and his veiled wife stand before him, hands twisted, eyes darting toward the doorway.

dialogue.text: He did not start with slogans. He started with listening, as tenants haltingly told him how planters forced indigo on their best land, fined them for refusing, and demanded illegal payments when synthetic dyes ruined the old profits.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने नारे नहीं लगाए, कान लगाए—किरायेदार लड़खड़ाती ज़ुबान से बताते गए कैसे साहब लोग उनकी बेहतरीन जमीन पर जबरन नील बोते, इनकार पर जुर्माना ठोकते, और कृत्रिम रंगों से मुनाफा गिरते ही अवैध वसूली करते।

panels.shot: close-up on Gandhi’s hand writing in a notebook, faint outline of trembling peasant in background
panels.action: A close view shows Gandhi’s steady hand moving across a small notebook, cramped English and Gujarati lines forming, while behind him the blurred figure of a peasant stands with head bowed.

dialogue.text: Each grievance became a line of ink: acreage forced under indigo, beatings, unpaid labour, bogus rent hikes, all carefully entered with names and dates that no official report could dismiss as rumour.

i18n.hi: हर शिकायत स्याही की लकीर बनी: कितनी ज़मीन पर जबरन नील, कितनी मार, मुफ्त मज़दूरी, झूठी किराया बढ़ोतरी—सब नाम और तारीख़ समेत, ताकि कोई हाकिमी रिपोर्ट इसे अफवाह कह कर टाल न सके।

panels.shot: medium shot in a district office verandah as a British officer hands Gandhi an order to leave, constables nearby
panels.action: On the verandah of the Motihari district office, a British magistrate in starched clothes hands a folded notice to Gandhi, while two Indian constables stand stiffly nearby and clerks glance up from their ledgers.

dialogue.text: The district authorities grew uneasy. An outsider, a barrister from South Africa, was roaming estates, taking notes. They served him an order: leave Champaran at once, or face prosecution.

i18n.hi: जिले के अफसर घबरा उठे। बाहर से आया, दक्षिण अफ्रीका का वकील, जमींदारियों में घूम रहा था, नोट लिख रहा था। उसे हुक्म मिला: फौरन चंपारण छोड़ो, वरना मुकदमा झेलो।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Gandhi holding the notice, calm expression, with villagers in background watching anxiously
panels.action: Gandhi stands outside, the notice open in his hand, eyes calm, as a small knot of villagers hover in the background, their faces tight with worry.

dialogue.speaker: Mahatma Gandhi
dialogue.text: I must disobey. My duty is to the peasants’ truth.

i18n.hi: मुझे आदेश मानना नहीं, सच के कर्ज़दार किसानों का साथ निभाना है।

panels.shot: interior courtroom wide shot with Gandhi in the dock, magistrate on bench, lawyers and villagers crowded in
panels.action: Inside a modest courtroom, the British magistrate sits on the raised bench, while Gandhi stands in the dock, small and erect, Indian lawyers in coats and dhotis nearby, and villagers crowding the back of the room.

dialogue.text: When they tried him for defying the order, he pleaded guilty, but not ashamed. The law, he said, could not command him to abandon men who had trusted him with their stories.

i18n.hi: जब हुक्म तोड़ने पर उस पर मुकदमा चला, उसने खुद को दोषी माना, पर शर्मिंदा नहीं। बोला, कानून उसे उन लोगों को छोड़ने का हुक्म नहीं दे सकता, जिन्होंने अपना दुख उसके हवाले किया है।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on Gandhi in the dock, slight low angle to emphasize quiet resolve
panels.action: The camera holds on Gandhi alone in the dock, head slightly tilted, hands loosely clasped, his expression gentle yet unyielding as the magistrate’s figure blurs in the distance.

dialogue.speaker: Mahatma Gandhi
dialogue.text: I submit to your penalty, but I cannot submit to injustice.

i18n.hi: दंड आपका, पर अन्याय आपकी अदालत भी नहीं चला सकती।

panels.shot: wide shot outside the courthouse as a crowd waits; an official emerges to announce postponement and no immediate sentencing
panels.action: Outside the courthouse, villagers and townspeople wait in the sun, some shaded by umbrellas, as an Indian court official steps out and raises his hand to announce that judgment is postponed and Gandhi is free for now.

dialogue.text: The case hung in the air. Officials hesitated to jail a man who broke the law so openly, yet so politely. They postponed sentence and quietly let him continue his work.

i18n.hi: मुकदमा宙 में अटक गया। अफसर एक ऐसे आदमी को कैद करने से झिझके, जो कानून तोड़ रहा था, पर शिष्टता से। सज़ा टाल दी गई, और चुपचाप उसे काम जारी रखने दिया गया।

panels.shot: group medium shot of Gandhi with Rajendra Prasad and other Indian lawyers seated on the ground around him, in discussion
panels.action: Under the shade of a tree, Gandhi sits with Rajendra Prasad and other local lawyers in coats and turbans, their shoes neatly lined aside, as they lean toward him in serious discussion.

dialogue.text: Gandhi then turned to organisation. He asked Bihar’s lawyers—Rajendra Prasad, Brajkishore Prasad and others—to set aside fees, live simply, and help record every tenant’s case with discipline.

i18n.hi: फिर गांधी ने संगठन संभाला। उन्होंने बिहार के वकीलों—राजेंद्र प्रसाद, ब्रजकिशोर प्रसाद व साथियों—से कहा, फीस छोड़ो, सादा जियो, और हर किरायेदार की कहानी अनुशासन से दर्ज करो।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot in a school courtyard, with multiple small groups of lawyers taking statements from peasants under Gandhi’s supervision
panels.action: In the courtyard of a village school, mats are spread in rows where lawyers sit with papers and pens, each surrounded by peasants giving statements, while Gandhi walks slowly among them, occasionally stopping to listen.

dialogue.text: Soon, the courtyard was a quiet factory of facts: thousands of statements gathered, checked, and sorted, turning scattered fear into a structured case against tinkathia.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही आंगन खामोश सच की फैक्टरी बना: हजारों बयान जुटे, परखे, छांटे गए—बिखरा हुआ डर, टिंकठिया के खिलाफ ठोस मुकदमे में बदल गया।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a planter’s bungalow verandah as Gandhi sits with a European planter, both seated, the planter stiff
panels.action: On the cool verandah of a planter’s bungalow, Gandhi sits upright on a cane chair opposite a European planter in a sun helmet, his posture stiff, the open garden stretching beyond.

dialogue.text: He visited planters too, hearing their side as they spoke of falling prices, debts, and the need to keep tenants tied, even as the world’s demand for natural indigo shrank.

i18n.hi: वे साहबों से भी मिले, उनकी दास्तान सुनी—गिरती कीमतें, कर्ज़, और यह ज़िद कि भले दुनिया को प्राकृतिक नील कम लगे, पर किरायेदारों को जकड़ा ही रखना है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Gandhi gently addressing peasants gathered outside, instructing them calmly, with a few policemen watching from afar
panels.action: Standing on a low platform outside a village, Gandhi addresses a cluster of peasants seated on the ground, one hand raised in a calming gesture, while a few policemen stand at a distance, observing.

dialogue.speaker: Mahatma Gandhi
dialogue.text: No violence, no threats. We only speak and write the truth.

i18n.hi: न हिंसा, न धमकी। हम बस सच कहेंगे और लिखेंगे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a government meeting room in Patna, with the Champaran enquiry committee seated at a long table, Gandhi among them
panels.action: In a high-ceilinged government room with tall windows, members of the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee sit around a long table strewn with files and notes, Gandhi among them, bareheaded and simple amid coats and ties.

dialogue.text: Under rising pressure, the provincial government formed an enquiry committee. Gandhi accepted a seat, carrying into the room not anger, but stacks of detailed testimonies.

i18n.hi: दबाव बढ़ा तो सूबे की सरकार ने जांच कमेटी बनाई। गांधी ने स्थान स्वीकार किया, कमरे में गुस्सा नहीं, बल्कि ढेरों तफ़सीली गवाही लेकर पहुंचे।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Gandhi speaking calmly across the table to a British official, pointing lightly to a page of evidence
panels.action: Gandhi leans slightly forward across the polished table, finger resting on a specific page, as a British official in spectacles listens, pen paused above his notebook.

dialogue.text: Patiently, he pressed for the tenants’ facts to be recognised in the official record: forced indigo, illegal exactions, coercive tactics, all documented in the committee’s formal report.

i18n.hi: धैर्य से उन्होंने ज़ोर दिया कि किरायेदारों के तथ्य सरकारी रिकॉर्ड में दर्ज हों: जबरन नील, अवैध वसूली, ज़बरदस्ती की चालें—सब कमेटी की आधिकारिक रिपोर्ट में उतारे गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a planter estate office where a clerk reads out new terms to tenants, with Gandhi absent but his influence felt
panels.action: Inside a planter estate office, an Indian clerk reads out new terms to a group of tenants, while the estate manager looks on, a map of fields on the wall and the old indigo vats lying unused outside.

dialogue.text: The committee’s recommendations did not overthrow the Raj, but they mattered: abolition of tinkathia, refund of part of illegal payments, and a path, slowly, for planters to withdraw from forced indigo.

i18n.hi: कमेटी की सिफारिशों ने राज नहीं गिराया, पर असर किया: टिंकठिया खत्म, कुछ अवैध वसूलियाँ लौटाना, और साहबों के लिए जबरन नील से धीरे-धीरे हटने की राह।

panels.shot: medium shot in a village setting where Gandhi sits among peasants and children, a simple makeshift school visible behind
panels.action: Back in a village, Gandhi sits on the ground with peasants and a few barefoot children, a makeshift school hut behind them with slates and chalk, as he speaks softly to a small circle.

dialogue.text: Even as legal reforms were drafted, he stayed to start schools, promote cleanliness, and urge tenants to shed the habits of fear that had grown alongside the indigo plants.

i18n.hi: कानूनी सुधार लिखते-लिखते भी वे रुके नहीं—स्कूल शुरू किए, सफाई पर ज़ोर दिया, और किरायेदारों से कहा, नील के पौधों के साथ पनपी डर की आदत छोड़ दो।

panels.shot: close-up of Gandhi in later years recalling Champaran, with a faint overlay of indigo fields in his mind’s eye
panels.action: In a later scene, Gandhi sits older and thinner, writing at a small desk, his face reflective, as faint, ghostly images of Champaran’s fields and huts seem to hover in the background.

dialogue.text: Years later, Gandhi would remember Champaran not as a dramatic victory, but as a quiet experiment where investigation, disciplined refusal, and negotiation showed how patient truth could bend even an empire’s paperwork.

i18n.hi: सालों बाद गांधी ने चंपारण को न बड़ी जीत कहा, न नाटक—बल्कि एक शांत प्रयोग, जहाँ जांच, अनुशासित अवज्ञा और बातचीत ने दिखाया कि धीरज वाला सच कैसे साम्राज्य की फाइलें भी मोड़ सकता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a quiet investigation turned indigo fear into a record the Raj could not ignore
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक शांत जांच ने नील के डर को ऐसे रिकॉर्ड में बदला जिसे राज नज़रअंदाज़ न कर सका
